positions.commentary: The speaker mentions that META's CAPEX jumped by 15 plus billion dollars over a two-year period, more than doubling from 2020 levels.

thesis: The episode argues that Meta is well-positioned in the AI arms race due to its successful infrastructure investments, aggressive CAPEX, and improved ad targeting which are driving high incremental operating margins. While the company faces significant losses from Reality Labs, the speaker contends that heavy investment in AI and the Metaverse is necessary to maintain long-term value and that the current investment cycle will likely continue indefinitely.

claims.claim: The speaker believes Meta is in a good position due to its successful AI infrastructure investments, improved ad targeting, and ability to grow revenue while controlling expenses.
claims.quote: And so again, this is part of the year of efficiency, continuing on. But this is also just a success that they've had in solving ATT and really leaning into AI in order to continue to just make the recommendations of ads better.

claims.claim: Meta's AI initiatives are driving tangible financial success, with revenue growing significantly against much lower expense growth, resulting in high incremental operating margins.
claims.quote: In 1Q24, it was a continuation of that theme. We saw that revenue grew 27% against expenses of just 6%. And so again, this is part of the year of efficiency, continuing on.

claims.claim: Meta is aggressively investing in AI infrastructure and increasing its CAPEX guidance to improve ad targeting and recommendation systems.
claims.quote: And in fact, they actually up their CAPX guidance. Now they're talking about doing 30 to 37 billion in CAPEX, a $2 billion increase on the high end from prior.

claims.claim: Meta's AI recommendation systems are now serving a large portion of content in both Facebook and Instagram feeds, enhancing user engagement.
claims.quote: And so they gave some numbers that now 30% of the Facebook feed is AI recommendations and 50% of the Instagram feed is now AI recommendations.

claims.claim: Meta is sitting in a good position in the AI arms race, having scooped up Nvidia chips when others were canceling orders.
claims.quote: And now, obviously, he looks like a real smart guy because no one else can get them. And it's kind of now an arms race. And so meta is sitting in kind of a good position here in terms of that.

claims.claim: The speaker believes META is investing heavily in AI infrastructure and the Metaverse, and that this investment cycle will likely continue indefinitely to maintain long-term value.
claims.quote: I don't see Mark Zuckerberg ever's not in taking cash flow of the business and investing in a new idea. So when people say, oh, if they stopped investing, the margins are this, I don't know how useful an exercise that is because it's unclear that will actually ever materialize.

claims.claim: The speaker argues that META's high CAPEX is necessary for growth and innovation, and that stopping investment would destroy the company's long-term terminal value.
claims.quote: I think if you stop investing and you stop trying to innovate on things, then the business, you're not going to have a long terminal value. You need to constantly be trying to trying new things.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that META's free cash flow conversion rate recovered to 74% in 2023 after dropping significantly in 2022, indicating a reversal of previous cash flow issues.
claims.quote: And then it essentially just reversed the next year. And so 2023, it was 74% LTM, it is still 74%. And so you do see that that free cash flow started to convert, which is what you want to see.

claims.claim: The speaker states that META generated $34 billion in free cash flow for the trailing twelve months when treating stock-based comp as a cash expense.
claims.quote: In total, LTM, they have free cash flow of $33.3.8 billion if you were to treat SBC as a cash expense. So $34 billion in free cash flow.

claims.claim: The speaker points out that META has $16 billion in losses from Reality Labs included in their trailing twelve-month financials.
